transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Um… well, I guess what finally scared me enough to come in is I’ve been hearing somebody call my name. Like from the hallway at home, and I’ll go look and nobody’s there. And once it happened at the warehouse too, which was embarrassing because I turned around like someone was right behind me.

It sounds real, like… like my husband standing next to me saying it. I keep thinking maybe it’s just the building noises or someone messing around, but it’s been getting to me.
Have you been using any drugs, including meth, cocaine, cannabis, or hallucinogens?

Um… no, not like that. I mean, I’ve been around people who do stuff—my cousin used to talk about mushrooms like it was some big spiritual thing, and I always thought, why would you want to see more weird things than are already in the world, you know?

But no, I’m not using meth or cocaine or anything. Cannabis… I don’t really do that either. I mean, maybe years ago at a party, but not now. I mostly just go to work, come home, try to keep things normal.
Do you believe someone is intentionally trying to communicate with you or target you through these voices?

I don’t know if it’s someone trying to, like… communicate. It doesn’t say anything really, it’s just my name. That’s what scares me, because it sounds so real—like my husband is standing right there in the hallway calling me.

And then it happened at work once, at the warehouse, and I turned around thinking somebody needed me, but nobody was there. I mean, in a warehouse there’s always noises, pallets and doors and people talking, so you try to explain it away, but… at home it’s different. It feels too clear to just be the house settling.
Have you had any hearing problems lately?

I don’t think so… I mean, not that I’ve noticed. Sometimes at the warehouse everything echoes, and those carts make that horrible squeal, so I’ll think I missed what somebody said—but everybody misses stuff in there, you know? My husband says I hear the TV fine, maybe too fine because I complain when the commercials get loud.

So… no, I haven’t had my hearing checked or anything recently, but I wouldn’t say I’m having hearing problems.
Have you felt confused or disoriented lately?

Confused? I mean… not like I don’t know where I am or anything. I get turned around sometimes if I’m tired, but who doesn’t, especially in those big aisles at work—everything looks the same when they move product around.

But disoriented… I don’t think so. I know where I am. I know the day mostly, unless it’s one of those weeks where the schedule gets weird. What do you mean exactly by confused?
Have you felt like your thoughts were not private anymore?

My thoughts not private… I don’t know. I mean, I don’t think people can hear what I’m thinking, if that’s what you mean. Sometimes I worry I said something out loud when I didn’t mean to, because at work I’m always talking to myself a little—like counting boxes or trying to remember what aisle I’m supposed to be in.

But my thoughts themselves… no, I haven’t really noticed that. Unless you mean something different by private?
Have you been seeing things that other people don’t seem to see?

Seeing things? No, not really… I mean, sometimes in the warehouse lighting, you catch a shadow and think it’s a person, but then it’s just one of those stacked pallets or a jacket hanging there. They move stuff around all the time, and the aisles—sorry, that’s not what you asked.

What scared me enough to come in wasn’t seeing things. It was hearing my name. Like from the hallway at home, clear as anything, and nobody’s there. It happened once at the warehouse too, and it sounded as real as my husband standing right next to me.
Have you had trouble keeping your thoughts organized when you talk?

Yeah… I think so. I’ll start trying to answer something simple and then my mind just jumps. Like I’ll be thinking about warehouse orders, then suddenly yarn colors—because I crochet sometimes—and then the bills, and then old family names from way back, and I lose what I was even saying.

It’s like everything is stacked too close together in my head, kind of like when the pallets are all crammed in and you’re trying to pull one thing but three other things come with it. I know that probably sounds silly, but yes, I have trouble staying organized when I talk sometimes.
Have you been needing much less sleep than usual?

Yes. For a while I was only sleeping maybe two or three hours, and then I’d wake up like I was ready to go, like I didn’t even need more. It felt like sleep was just… in the way, like wasting time I needed for things I was working on.

I’d get up and start on projects, or make lists, or try to organize stuff, and then one thing would turn into another. Like if I was sorting something, then I’d remember something else that needed doing, and suddenly it’s morning. But I didn’t feel tired the way I should have.
During the time you were sleeping only two or three hours, did you also feel unusually happy or high?

Yeah… at first I did. Not just happy exactly, more like fired up. Like I had all this energy and I could finally get my craft business going right, and get the house running the way it should, with rules that made sense.

And then if my husband said something small—like, not even mean, just a comment—I’d snap at him. It felt like he was trying to slow me down or get in my way. I’d get so mad so fast, and then I’d go right back to thinking I had everything figured out.
During those high-energy periods, did you feel you had special powers or an unusually important mission?

I don’t know if I’d call it special powers, exactly… but I did feel like I had this big important thing I was supposed to do.

I got really convinced I could turn my crafts into a real retirement business right away, like not just selling a few things here and there, but something solid. I was thinking, “This is it, this is how I fix things for us.” And I thought once everyone saw the plan, they’d understand I’d figured out the perfect way for our family.

I mean, I know people make crafts all the time, and I’d start thinking about yarn prices and displays and names for the shop, and then what my aunt used to make, and it all felt connected somehow. But at the time it felt very important, like I was the one who finally saw it clearly.
Did the times when you heard your name happen only when you were in that fired-up, sleeping-very-little state?

Yes, I think so. It was during that stretch when I was barely sleeping and I was talking all the time, just going from one thing to the next, trying to fix everything.

I remember hearing my name then, and it scared me some, but I also had so much going on in my head. Before all that, I don’t remember anything like that. And then later, when I got really low and kind of pulled back from everybody, I wasn’t hearing my name or believing things like that. It seemed tied to that fired-up time.
Have you ever had a period lasting at least two weeks when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?

Yes… I mean, after all that running around and arguing, it was like I just dropped. I’d get this heavy, empty feeling, and I’d sit at the kitchen table and cry over nothing.

And I know everybody cries sometimes, like when the bills pile up or the sink’s full of dishes—ours always seems to be full no matter what I do—but this felt different. Like I couldn’t get myself back. It was most of the day, a lot of days in a row.
